If we trace over systems A′​B′A^{\prime}B^{\prime}, the fidelity only goes up, so consider that the state above becomes as follows under this partial trace:

1d∑i|i⟩⟨i|B⊗TrA′​B′{(VA′​B′i)†ℛE→A​A′​E(TrA^′{VA^′​B′iρA^′​B′​E(VA^′​B′i)†})VA′​B′i}\displaystyle\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i}\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{B}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\left\{\left(V_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\right)^{{\dagger}}\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AA^{\prime}E}\left(\operatorname{Tr}_{\hat{A}^{\prime}}\left\{V_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\rho_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}E}\left(V_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\right)^{{\dagger}}\right\}\right)V_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\right\}
=1d∑i|i⟩⟨i|B⊗TrA′​B′{ℛE→A​A′​E(TrA^′{VA^′​B′iρA^′​B′​E(VA^′​B′i)†})}\displaystyle=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i}\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{B}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\left\{\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AA^{\prime}E}\left(\operatorname{Tr}_{\hat{A}^{\prime}}\left\{V_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\rho_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}E}\left(V_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\right)^{{\dagger}}\right\}\right)\right\} (5.83)
=1d∑i|i⟩⟨i|B⊗TrA′{ℛE→A​A′​E(TrA^′​B′{VA^′​B′iρA^′​B′​E(VA^′​B′i)†})}\displaystyle=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i}\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{B}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{A^{\prime}}\left\{\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AA^{\prime}E}\left(\operatorname{Tr}_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\left\{V_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\rho_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}E}\left(V_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{i}\right)^{{\dagger}}\right\}\right)\right\} (5.84)
=1d∑i|i⟩⟨i|B⊗TrA′{ℛE→A​A′​E(TrA^′​B′{ρA^′​B′​E})}\displaystyle=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i}\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{B}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{A^{\prime}}\left\{\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AA^{\prime}E}\left(\operatorname{Tr}_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\left\{\rho_{\hat{A}^{\prime}B^{\prime}E}\right\}\right)\right\} (5.85)
=1d∑i|i⟩⟨i|B⊗TrA′{ℛE→A​A′​E(ρE)}\displaystyle=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i}\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{B}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{A^{\prime}}\left\{\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AA^{\prime}E}\left(\rho_{E}\right)\right\} (5.86)
=πB⊗ℛE→A​E​(ρE),\displaystyle=\pi_{B}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{E}\right), (5.87)

where πB\pi_{B} is a maximally mixed state on system BB. So an upper bound on (5.80) is given by

F⁡(ΦA​B⊗ρE,πB⊗ℛE→A​E​(ρE))\displaystyle F\left(\Phi_{AB}\otimes\rho_{E},\pi_{B}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{E}\right)\right) ≤F⁡(ΦA​B,πB⊗ℛE→A​(ρE))\displaystyle\leq F\left(\Phi_{AB},\pi_{B}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow A}\left(\rho_{E}\right)\right) (5.88)
=1/d2.\displaystyle=1/d^{2}. (5.89)

Since this upper bound is universal for any recovery map and any extension of the original state, we obtain the following inequality:

supγA​B​A′​B′​E:γA​B​A′​B′=TrE⁡{γA​B​A′​B′​E}F(AA′;BB′|E)γ≤1/d2.\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\gamma_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}E}:\\ \gamma_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{E}\left\{\gamma_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}E}\right\}\end{subarray}}F\left(AA^{\prime};BB^{\prime}|E\right)_{\gamma}\leq 1/d^{2}. (5.90)

After taking a negative logarithm, we recover the statement of the proposition.  

Proposition 24 (Subadditivity / Supermultiplicativity)

Let ωA1​B1​A2​B2≡ρA1​B1⊗σA2​B2\omega_{A_{1}B_{1}A_{2}B_{2}}\equiv\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}}\otimes\sigma_{A_{2}B_{2}}. Then

EFsq​(A1​A2,B1​B2)ω≤EFsq​(A1,B1)ρ+EFsq​(A2,B2)σ,E_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1}A_{2};B_{1}B_{2}\right)_{\omega}\leq E_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1};B_{1}\right)_{\rho}+E_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{2};B_{2}\right)_{\sigma}, (5.91)

which is equivalent to

Fsq​(A1,B1)ρ⋅Fsq​(A2,B2)τ≤Fsq​(A1​A2,B1​B2)ρ⊗τ.F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1};B_{1}\right)_{\rho}\cdot F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{2};B_{2}\right)_{\tau}\leq F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1}A_{2};B_{1}B_{2}\right)_{\rho\otimes\tau}. (5.92)

Proof. Let ρA1​B1​E1\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}E_{1}} be an extension of ρA1​B1\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}} and let τA2​B2​E2\tau_{A_{2}B_{2}E_{2}} be an extension of τA2​B2\tau_{A_{2}B_{2}}. Let ℛE1→A1​E11\mathcal{R}_{E_{1}\rightarrow A_{1}E_{1}}^{1} and ℛE2→A2​E22\mathcal{R}_{E_{2}\rightarrow A_{2}E_{2}}^{2} be recovery maps. Then

F⁡(ρA1​B1​E1,ℛE1→A1​E11​(ρB1​E1))⋅F⁡(τA2​B2​E2,ℛE2→A2​E22​(τB2​E2))\displaystyle F\left(\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}E_{1}},\mathcal{R}_{E_{1}\rightarrow A_{1}E_{1}}^{1}\left(\rho_{B_{1}E_{1}}\right)\right)\cdot F\left(\tau_{A_{2}B_{2}E_{2}},\mathcal{R}_{E_{2}\rightarrow A_{2}E_{2}}^{2}\left(\tau_{B_{2}E_{2}}\right)\right)
=F⁡(ρA1​B1​E1⊗τA2​B2​E2,ℛE1→A1​E11​(ρB1​E1)⊗ℛE2→A2​E22​(τB2​E2))\displaystyle=F\left(\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}E_{1}}\otimes\tau_{A_{2}B_{2}E_{2}},\mathcal{R}_{E_{1}\rightarrow A_{1}E_{1}}^{1}\left(\rho_{B_{1}E_{1}}\right)\otimes\mathcal{R}_{E_{2}\rightarrow A_{2}E_{2}}^{2}\left(\tau_{B_{2}E_{2}}\right)\right) (5.93)
≤supωA1​A2​B1​B2​EsupℛE→A1​A2​E{F⁡(ωA1​A2​B1​B2​E,ℛE→A1​A2​E​(ωB1​B2​E)):ρA1​B1⊗τA2​B2=TrE⁡{ωA1​A2​B1​B2​E}}\displaystyle\leq\sup_{\omega_{A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}E}}\sup_{\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow A_{1}A_{2}E}}\left\{F\left(\omega_{A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}E},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow A_{1}A_{2}E}\left(\omega_{B_{1}B_{2}E}\right)\right):\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}}\otimes\tau_{A_{2}B_{2}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{E}\left\{\omega_{A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}E}\right\}\right\} (5.94)
=Fsq​(A1​A2,B1​B2)ρ⊗τ\displaystyle=F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1}A_{2};B_{1}B_{2}\right)_{\rho\otimes\tau} (5.95)

Since the inequality holds for all extensions ρA1​B1​E1\rho_{A_{1}B_{1}E_{1}} and τA2​B2​E2\tau_{A_{2}B_{2}E_{2}} and recovery maps ℛE1→A1​E11\mathcal{R}_{E_{1}\rightarrow A_{1}E_{1}}^{1} and ℛE2→A2​E22\mathcal{R}_{E_{2}\rightarrow A_{2}E_{2}}^{2}, we can conclude that

Fsq​(A1,B1)ρ⋅Fsq​(A2,B2)τ≤Fsq​(A1​A2,B1​B2)ρ⊗τF^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1};B_{1}\right)_{\rho}\cdot F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{2};B_{2}\right)_{\tau}\leq F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A_{1}A_{2};B_{1}B_{2}\right)_{\rho\otimes\tau} (5.96)

By taking negative logarithms and dividing by 1/2, we arrive at the subadditivity statement for EFsqE_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}.  

Proposition 25 (Continuity)

The geometric squashed entanglement is a continuous function of its input. That is, given two bipartite states ρA​B\rho_{AB} and σA​B\sigma_{AB} such that F⁡(ρA​B,σA​B)≥1−εF\left(\rho_{AB},\sigma_{AB}\right)\geq 1-\varepsilon where ε∈[0,1]\varepsilon\in\left[0,1\right], then the following inequalities hold

|Fsq​(A,B)ρ−Fsq​(A,B)σ|\displaystyle\left|F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\sigma}\right| ≤8​ε,\displaystyle\leq 8\sqrt{\varepsilon}, (5.97)
|EFsq​(A,B)ρ−EFsq​(A,B)σ|\displaystyle\left|E_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-E_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\sigma}\right| ≤4​|A|2​ε.\displaystyle\leq 4\left|A\right|^{2}\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (5.98)

Proof. One of the main tools for our proof is the purified distance [TCR10, Definition 4], defined for two quantum states as

P⁡(ρ,σ)≡1−F⁡(ρ,σ),P\left(\rho,\sigma\right)\equiv\sqrt{1-F\left(\rho,\sigma\right)}, (5.99)

and which for our case implies that

P⁡(ρA​B,σA​B)≤ε.P\left(\rho_{AB},\sigma_{AB}\right)\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (5.100)

Letting σA​B​E\sigma_{ABE} be an arbitrary extension of σA​B\sigma_{AB}, [TCR10, Corollary 9] implies that there exists an extension ρA​B​E\rho_{ABE} of ρA​B\rho_{AB} such that

P⁡(ρA​B​E,σA​B​E)=P⁡(ρA​B,σA​B)≤ε.P\left(\rho_{ABE},\sigma_{ABE}\right)=P\left(\rho_{AB},\sigma_{AB}\right)\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (5.101)

Let ℛE→A​E\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE} be an arbitrary recovery map. Then the above and monotonicity of the purified distance under quantum operations [TCR10, Lemma 7] imply that

P⁡(ℛE→A​E​(ρB​E),ℛE→A​E​(σB​E))≤P⁡(ρA​B​E,σA​B​E)≤ε.P\left(\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{BE}\right),\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right)\leq P\left(\rho_{ABE},\sigma_{ABE}\right)\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (5.102)

So consider that the triangle inequality for purified distance [TCR10, Lemma 5] implies that

P⁡(ρA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(ρB​E))\displaystyle P\left(\rho_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{BE}\right)\right) ≤P⁡(ρA​B​E,σA​B​E)+P⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E))\displaystyle\leq P\left(\rho_{ABE},\sigma_{ABE}\right)+P\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right)
+P⁡(ℛE→A​E​(σB​E),ℛE→A​E​(ρB​E))\displaystyle\ \ \ \ \ +P\left(\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right),\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{BE}\right)\right) (5.103)
≤ε+P⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E))+ε\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon}+P\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right)+\sqrt{\varepsilon} (5.104)
=P⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E))+2​ε.\displaystyle=P\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right)+2\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (5.105)

This is equivalent to

1−F⁡(ρA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(ρB​E))≤1−F⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E))+2​ε\sqrt{1-F\left(\rho_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{BE}\right)\right)}\leq\sqrt{1-F\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right)}+2\sqrt{\varepsilon} (5.106)

which upon squaring gives

1−F⁡(ρA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(ρB​E))≤1−F⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E))+8​ε,1-F\left(\rho_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{BE}\right)\right)\leq 1-F\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right)+8\sqrt{\varepsilon}, (5.107)

where we used that F⁡(ρ,σ)∈[0,1]F\left(\rho,\sigma\right)\in\left[0,1\right] and ε≤ε\varepsilon\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon} for ε∈[0,1]\varepsilon\in\left[0,1\right]. This in turn implies the following inequality

F⁡(ρA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(ρB​E))+8​ε≥F⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E)).F\left(\rho_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\rho_{BE}\right)\right)+8\sqrt{\varepsilon}\geq F\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right). (5.108)

By taking a supremum, we find that

Fsq​(A,B)ρ+8​ε≥F⁡(σA​B​E,ℛE→A​E​(σB​E)).F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}+8\sqrt{\varepsilon}\geq F\left(\sigma_{ABE},\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE}\left(\sigma_{BE}\right)\right). (5.109)

Since the extension of σA​B\sigma_{AB} and the recovery map ℛE→A​E\mathcal{R}_{E\rightarrow AE} were arbitrary, it follows that

Fsq​(A,B)ρ+8​ε≥Fsq​(A,B)σ.F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}+8\sqrt{\varepsilon}\geq F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\sigma}. (5.110)

By a similar argument (but tailoring an extension of σA​B​E\sigma_{ABE} to an arbitrary extension of ρA​B\rho_{AB}), we can conclude the other inequality

Fsq​(A,B)σ+8​ε≥Fsq​(A,B)ρ,F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\sigma}+8\sqrt{\varepsilon}\geq F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}, (5.111)

which gives us (5.97).

By dividing (5.110) by Fsq​(A,B)ρF^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho} and taking a logarithm, we find that

log⁡(Fsq​(A,B)σFsq​(A,B)ρ)\displaystyle\log\left(\frac{F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\sigma}}{F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}}\right) ≤log⁡(1+8​εFsq​(A,B)ρ)\displaystyle\leq\log\left(1+\frac{8\sqrt{\varepsilon}}{F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}}\right) (5.112)
≤8​εFsq​(A,B)ρ\displaystyle\leq\frac{8\sqrt{\varepsilon}}{F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}} (5.113)
≤|A|2​8​ε.\displaystyle\leq\left|A\right|^{2}8\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (5.114)

where we used that log⁡(x+1)≤x\log\left(x+1\right)\leq x and the dimension bound from Proposition 7. Applying this to the other inequality in (5.111) gives that

log⁡(Fsq​(A,B)ρFsq​(A,B)σ)≤|A|2​8​ε,\log\left(\frac{F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}}{F^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\sigma}}\right)\leq\left|A\right|^{2}8\sqrt{\varepsilon}, (5.115)

from which we can conclude (5.98) upon dividing both sides by 1/2.  

6 Fidelity of measurement recovery

In this section, we propose an alternative measure of quantum correlations, the surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity, which follows the original motivation behind the quantum discord [OZ01]. However, our measure has a clear operational meaning in the “one-shot” setting, being based on how well one recover a bipartite quantum state if one system is measured. We begin by recalling the definition of the quantum discord and proceed from there with the motivation behind the newly proposed measure.

Definition 26 (Quantum discord)

The quantum discord of a bipartite state ρA​B\rho_{AB} is defined as the difference between the quantum mutual information of ρA​B\rho_{AB} and the classical correlation [HV01] of ρA​B\rho_{AB}:

D​(A¯,B)ρ\displaystyle D\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} ≡I​(A,B)ρ−sup{Λx}I​(X,B)σ\displaystyle\equiv I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-\sup_{\left\{\Lambda^{x}\right\}}I\left(X;B\right)_{\sigma} (6.1)
=inf{Λx}[I​(A,B)ρ−I​(X,B)σ],\displaystyle=\inf_{\left\{\Lambda^{x}\right\}}\left[I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-I\left(X;B\right)_{\sigma}\right], (6.2)

where {Λx}\left\{\Lambda^{x}\right\} is a POVM with Λx≥0\Lambda^{x}\geq 0 for all xx and ∑xΛx=I\sum_{x}\Lambda^{x}=I and σX​B\sigma_{XB} is defined as

σX​B≡∑x|x⟩⟨x|X⊗TrA{ΛAxρA​B}.\sigma_{XB}\equiv\sum_{x}\left|x\right\rangle\left\langle x\right|_{X}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{A}\left\{\Lambda_{A}^{x}\rho_{AB}\right\}. (6.3)

We now recall some developments from [BSW14] and [SBW14]. Let ℳA→X\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X} denote the following measurement map:

ℳA→X(ωA)≡∑xTr{ΛAxωA}|x⟩⟨x|X.\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\omega_{A}\right)\equiv\sum_{x}\operatorname{Tr}\left\{\Lambda_{A}^{x}\omega_{A}\right\}\left|x\right\rangle\left\langle x\right|_{X}. (6.4)

Using this, we can write (6.3) asσX​B=ℳA→X​(ρA​B)\ \sigma_{XB}=\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\rho_{AB}\right). Now, to every measurement map ℳA→X\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}, we can find an isometric extension of it with the following form:

UA→X​Eℳ|ψ⟩A≡∑x|x⟩X|x,y⟩E⟨φx,y|A|ψ⟩A,U_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\left|\psi\right\rangle_{A}\equiv\sum_{x}\left|x\right\rangle_{X}\left|x,y\right\rangle_{E}\left\langle\varphi_{x,y}\right|_{A}\left|\psi\right\rangle_{A}, (6.5)

where the vectors {|φx,y⟩A}\left\{\left|\varphi_{x,y}\right\rangle_{A}\right\} are part of a rank-one refinement of the POVM {ΛAx}\left\{\Lambda_{A}^{x}\right\}:

ΛAx=∑y|φx,y⟩⟨φx,y|.\Lambda_{A}^{x}=\sum_{y}\left|\varphi_{x,y}\right\rangle\left\langle\varphi_{x,y}\right|. (6.6)

Thus,

ℳA→X​(ωA)=TrE⁡{𝒰A→X​Eℳ​(ωA)},\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\omega_{A}\right)=\operatorname{Tr}_{E}\left\{\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\left(\omega_{A}\right)\right\}, (6.7)

where

𝒰A→X​Eℳ​(ωA)≡UA→X​Eℳ​(ωA)​(UA→X​Eℳ)†.\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\left(\omega_{A}\right)\equiv U_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\left(\omega_{A}\right)\left(U_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\right)^{{\dagger}}. (6.8)

Let σX​E​B\sigma_{XEB} denote the following state:

σX​E​B=𝒰A→X​Eℳ​(ρA​B).\sigma_{XEB}=\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\left(\rho_{AB}\right). (6.9)

We can use the above development to rewrite the objective function of the quantum discord in (6.2) as follows:

I​(A,B)ρ−I​(X,B)σ\displaystyle I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-I\left(X;B\right)_{\sigma} =I​(X​E,B)σ−I​(X,B)σ\displaystyle=I\left(XE;B\right)_{\sigma}-I\left(X;B\right)_{\sigma} (6.10)
=I​(E;B|X)σ.\displaystyle=I\left(E;B|X\right)_{\sigma}. (6.11)

So this means that we can rewrite the discord in terms of the conditional mutual information as

D⁡(A¯,B)=inf{Λx}I​(E;B|X)σ,D\left(\overline{A};B\right)=\inf_{\left\{\Lambda^{x}\right\}}I\left(E;B|X\right)_{\sigma}, (6.12)

with the state σX​E​B\sigma_{XEB} understood as described above, as arising from an isometric extension of a measurement map applied to the state ρA​B\rho_{AB}. We are now in a position to define the surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity:

Definition 27 (Surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity)

We define the following information quantity:

DF​(A¯,B)ρ≡inf{Λx}IF​(E;B|X)σ,D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}\equiv\inf_{\left\{\Lambda^{x}\right\}}I_{F}\left(E;B|X\right)_{\sigma}, (6.13)

where we have simply substituted the conditional mutual information in (6.12) with IFI_{F}. Writing out the right-hand side of (6.13) carefully, we find that

DF(A¯;B)=−logsupUA→X​Eℳ,ℛX→X​EF(𝒰A→X​Eℳ(ρA​B),ℛX→X​E(ℳA→X(ρA​B))),D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)=-\log\sup_{U_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}},\mathcal{R}_{X\rightarrow XE}}F\left(\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\left(\rho_{AB}\right),\mathcal{R}_{X\rightarrow XE}\left(\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\right), (6.14)

where ℳA→X\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X} is defined in (6.4), UA→X​EℳU_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}} is defined in (6.5), and 𝒰A→X​Eℳ\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}} is defined in (6.8).

This quantity has a similar interpretation as the original discord, as summarized in the following quote from [OZ01]:

“A vanishing discord can be considered as an indicator of the superselection rule, or — in the case of interest — its value is a measure of the efficiency of einselection. When [the discord] is large for any measurement, a lot of information is missed and destroyed by any measurement on the apparatus alone, but when [the discord] is small almost all the information about [the system] that exists in the [system–apparatus] correlations is locally recoverable from the state of the apparatus.”

Indeed, exploiting the invariance of fidelity under isometries gives a simple rewriting of (6.14):

DF​(A¯,B)\displaystyle D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) =−logsupUA→X​Eℳ,ℛX→X​EF(ρA​B,(𝒰A→X​Eℳ)†(ℛX→X​E(ℳA→X(ρA​B))))\displaystyle=-\log\sup_{U_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}},\mathcal{R}_{X\rightarrow XE}}F\left(\rho_{AB},\left(\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow XE}^{\mathcal{M}}\right)^{{\dagger}}\left(\mathcal{R}_{X\rightarrow XE}\left(\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\right)\right) (6.15)
=−logsupℳA→X,𝒫X→AF(ρA​B,(𝒫X→A(ℳA→X(ρA​B)))).\displaystyle=-\log\sup_{\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X},\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}}F\left(\rho_{AB},\left(\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}\left(\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\right)\right). (6.16)

The last line follows the interpretation given in the quote above: the measurement map ℳA→X\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X} is performed on the AA system of the state ρA​B\rho_{AB}, which is followed by a recovery map 𝒫X→A\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A} that attempts to recover the AA system from the state of the measuring apparatus. Since the measurement map has a classical output, any recovery map acting on such a classical system is equivalent to a preparation map. So the quantity DF​(A¯,B)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) captures how difficult it is to recover the full bipartite state after some measurement is performed on it, following the original spirit of the quantum discord. However, the quantity DF​(A¯,B)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) defined above has the advantage of being a “one-shot” measure, given that the fidelity has a clear operational meaning in a “one-shot” setting. If DF​(A¯,B)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) is near to zero, then F⁡(ρA​B,(𝒫X→A​(ℳA→X​(ρA​B))))F\left(\rho_{AB},\left(\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}\left(\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\right)\right) is close to one, so that it is possible to recover the system AA by performing a recovery map on the state of the apparatus. Conversely, if DF​(A¯,B)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) is far from zero, then the measurement recovery fidelity is far from one, so that it is not possible to recover system AA from the state of the measuring apparatus.

Exploiting the observation that any entanglement breaking channel can be written as a concatenation of a measurement map with a preparation map [HSR03], we can rewrite DF​(A¯,B)ρD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} once again, this time seeing that it captures how close ρA​B\rho_{AB} is to being a fixed point of an entanglement-breaking channel:

DF(A¯;B)ρ=−logsupℰAF(ρA​B,ℰA(ρA​B)),D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}=-\log\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right), (6.17)

where the optimization is over the convex set of entanglement breaking channels. This observation leads to the following proposition, which characterizes quantum states with discord nearly equal to zero.

Proposition 28 (Approximate faithfulness)

A bipartite quantum state ρA​B\rho_{AB} has quantum discord nearly equal to zero if and only if it is an approximate fixed point of an entanglement breaking channel. More precisely, we have the following: If there exists an entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} and ε∈[0,1]\varepsilon\in\left[0,1\right] such that

‖ρA​B−ℰA​(ρA​B)‖1≤ε,\left\|\rho_{AB}-\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right\|_{1}\leq\varepsilon, (6.18)

then the quantum discord D​(A¯,B)ρD\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} obeys the following bound

D​(A¯,B)ρ≤4​h2​(ε)+8​ε​log⁡|A|,D\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}\leq 4h_{2}\left(\varepsilon\right)+8\varepsilon\log\left|A\right|, (6.19)

where h2​(ε)h_{2}\left(\varepsilon\right) is the binary entropy with the property that limε↘0h2​(ε)=0\lim_{\varepsilon\searrow 0}h_{2}\left(\varepsilon\right)=0. Conversely, if the quantum discord D​(A¯,B)ρD\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} obeys the following bound for ε∈[0,1]\varepsilon\in\left[0,1\right]:

D​(A¯,B)ρ≤ε,D\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}\leq\varepsilon, (6.20)

then there exists an entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} such that

‖ρA​B−ℰA​(ρA​B)‖1≤2​ε.\left\|\rho_{AB}-\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right\|_{1}\leq 2\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (6.21)

Proof. We begin by proving (6.18)-(6.19). Since any entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} consists of a measurement map ℳA→X\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X} followed by a preparation map 𝒫X→A\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}, we can write ℰA=𝒫X→A∘ℳA→X\mathcal{E}_{A}=\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}\circ\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}. Then consider that

D​(A¯,B)ρ\displaystyle D\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} =I​(A,B)ρ−sup{Λx}I​(X,B)σ\displaystyle=I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-\sup_{\left\{\Lambda^{x}\right\}}I\left(X;B\right)_{\sigma} (6.22)
≤I​(A,B)ρ−I​(X,B)ℳ⁡(ρ)\displaystyle\leq I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-I\left(X;B\right)_{\mathcal{M}\left(\rho\right)} (6.23)
≤I​(A,B)ρ−I​(A,B)𝒫∘ℳ⁡(ρ)\displaystyle\leq I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-I\left(A;B\right)_{\mathcal{P}\circ\mathcal{M}\left(\rho\right)} (6.24)
=I​(A,B)ρ−I​(A,B)ℰ⁡(ρ)\displaystyle=I\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}-I\left(A;B\right)_{\mathcal{E}\left(\rho\right)} (6.25)
≤4​h2​(ε)+8​ε​log⁡|A|.\displaystyle\leq 4h_{2}\left(\varepsilon\right)+8\varepsilon\log\left|A\right|. (6.26)

The first inequality follows because the measurement given by ℳA→X\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X} is not necessarily optimal. The second inequality is a consequence of the quantum data processing inequality, in which quantum mutual information is non-increasing under the local operation 𝒫X→A\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}. The last equality follows because ℰA=𝒫X→A∘ℳA→X\mathcal{E}_{A}=\mathcal{P}_{X\rightarrow A}\circ\mathcal{M}_{A\rightarrow X}. The last inequality is a consequence of the Alicki-Fannes inequality [AF04].

We now prove (6.20)-(6.21). The Fawzi-Renner inequality I​(A;B|C)ρ≥−log⁡F​(A;B|C)ρI(A;B|C)_{\rho}\geq-\log F(A;B|C)_{\rho} which holds for any tripartite state ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} [FR14], combined with other observations recalled in this section connecting discord with conditional mutual information, gives us that there exists an entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} such that

D​(A¯,B)ρ\displaystyle D\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} ≥−log⁡F⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))\displaystyle\geq-\log F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right) (6.27)
≥−log⁡(1−14​‖ρA​B−ℰA​(ρA​B)‖12)\displaystyle\geq-\log\left(1-\frac{1}{4}\left\|\rho_{AB}-\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right\|_{1}^{2}\right) (6.28)
≥14​‖ρA​B−ℰA​(ρA​B)‖12,\displaystyle\geq\frac{1}{4}\left\|\rho_{AB}-\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right\|_{1}^{2}, (6.29)

where the second inequality follows from well known relations between trace distance and fidelity [FvdG98] and the last from −log⁡(1−x)≥x-\log\left(1-x\right)\geq x, valid for x≤1x\leq 1. This is sufficient to conclude (6.20)-(6.21).  

The main conclusion we can take from Proposition 28 is that quantum states with discord nearly equal to zero are such that they are recoverable after performing some measurement on one share of them, making precise the quote from [OZ01] given above. In prior work [Hay06, Lemma 8.12], quantum states with discord exactly equal to zero were characterized as being entirely classical on the system being measured, but this condition is perhaps too restrictive for characterizing states with discord approximately equal to zero.

We now establish some properties of the surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity:

Proposition 29 (Invariance under local isometries)

DF​(A¯,B)ρD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} is invariant under local isometries, in the sense that

DF​(A¯,B)ρ=DF​(A′¯,B′)σ,D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}=D_{F}(\overline{A^{\prime}};B^{\prime})_{\sigma}, (6.30)

where

σA′​B′≡(𝒰A→A′⊗𝒱B→B′)​(ρA​B)\sigma_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\equiv\left(\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow A^{\prime}}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{B\rightarrow B^{\prime}}\right)\left(\rho_{AB}\right) (6.31)

and 𝒰A→A′\mathcal{U}_{A\rightarrow A^{\prime}} and 𝒱B→B′\mathcal{V}_{B\rightarrow B^{\prime}} are isometric CPTP maps.

Proof. Let ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} be some entanglement-breaking channel and let UAU_{A} and VBV_{B} denote the local isometries (for simplicity, we suppress the fact that they can map to systems of size different from their inputs). Then from invariance of fidelity under isometries, we find that

F⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))\displaystyle F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)
=F⁡((UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†,(UA⊗VB)​(ℰA​(ρA​B))​(UA⊗VB)†)\displaystyle=F\left(\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\rho_{AB}\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}},\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\left(\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}}\right) (6.32)
=F⁡((UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†,UA​(ℰA​(UA†​([(UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†])​UA))​UA†)\displaystyle=F\left(\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\rho_{AB}\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}},U_{A}\left(\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(U_{A}^{{\dagger}}\left(\left[\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\rho_{AB}\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}}\right]\right)U_{A}\right)\right)U_{A}^{{\dagger}}\right) (6.33)
≤supℰAF⁡((UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†,ℰA​([(UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†]))\displaystyle\leq\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\rho_{AB}\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\left[\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\rho_{AB}\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}}\right]\right)\right) (6.34)

Since the inequality is true for any map ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A}, we find after applying a negative logarithm that

DF​(A¯,B)ρ≥DF​(A¯,B)(𝒰⊗𝒱)​(ρ)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}\geq D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\left(\mathcal{U}\otimes\mathcal{V}\right)\left(\rho\right)} (6.35)

With essentially the same proof (by redefining ρA​B\rho_{AB} to be (UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)\rho_{AB}\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}} and taking UA⊗VBU_{A}\otimes V_{B} to be (UA⊗VB)†\left(U_{A}\otimes V_{B}\right)^{{\dagger}}), we find that

DF​(A¯,B)(U⊗V)​ρ​(U⊗V)†≥DF​(A¯,B)ρ,D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\left(U\otimes V\right)\rho\left(U\otimes V\right)^{{\dagger}}}\geq D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}, (6.36)

which gives the statement of the proposition.  

Proposition 30 (Exact faithfulness)

The surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity DF​(A¯,B)ρD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} is equal to zero if and only if ρA​B\rho_{AB} is a classical-quantum state, having the form

ρA​B=∑xpX(x)|x⟩⟨x|A⊗ρBx,\rho_{AB}=\sum_{x}p_{X}\left(x\right)\left|x\right\rangle\left\langle x\right|_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}^{x}, (6.37)

for some orthonormal basis {|x⟩}\left\{\left|x\right\rangle\right\}, probability distribution pX​(x)p_{X}\left(x\right), and states {ρBx}\left\{\rho_{B}^{x}\right\}.

Proof. Suppose that the state is classical-quantum. Then it is a fixed point of the entanglement breaking map ∑x|x⟩⟨x|A(⋅)|x⟩⟨x|A\sum_{x}\left|x\right\rangle\left\langle x\right|_{A}\left(\cdot\right)\left|x\right\rangle\left\langle x\right|_{A}, so that the fidelity of measurement recovery is equal to one and its suprisal is equal to zero. On the other hand, suppose that DF​(A¯,B)ρ=0D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}=0. Then this means that there exists an entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} of which ρA​B\rho_{AB} is a fixed point (since F⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))=1F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)=1 is equivalent to ρA​B=ℰA​(ρA​B)\rho_{AB}=\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)), and furthermore, applying the fixed point projection

ℰA¯≡limK→∞1K​∑k=1KℰAk\overline{\mathcal{E}_{A}}\equiv\lim_{K\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathcal{E}_{A}^{k} (6.38)

leaves ρA​B\rho_{AB} invariant. The map ℰA¯\overline{\mathcal{E}_{A}} has been characterized in [FNW14, Theorem 5.3] to be an entanglement breaking channel of the following form:

ℰA¯​(⋅)=∑iTr⁡{Mi​(⋅)}​σi,\overline{\mathcal{E}_{A}}\left(\cdot\right)=\sum_{i}\operatorname{Tr}\left\{M_{i}\left(\cdot\right)\right\}\sigma_{i}, (6.39)

where the states σi\sigma_{i} have orthogonal support. Applying this channel to ρA​B\rho_{AB} then gives a classical-quantum state, and since ρA​B\rho_{AB} is invariant under the action of this channel to begin with, it must have been classical-quantum from the start.  

Proposition 31 (Dimension bound)

The surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity obeys the following dimension bound:

DF​(A¯,B)ρ≤2​log⁡|A|,D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}\leq 2\log\left|A\right|, (6.40)

or equivalently,

supℰAF⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))≥1|A|2.\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\geq\frac{1}{\left|A\right|^{2}}. (6.41)

Proof. The idea behind the proof is to consider an entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} that traces out the input and replaces with the maximally mixed state. Furthermore, let ψA​B​C\psi_{ABC} be a purification of ρA​B\rho_{AB}. We then find that

DF​(A¯,B)ρ\displaystyle D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} ≤−log⁡F⁡(ρA​B,πA⊗ρB)\displaystyle\leq-\log F\left(\rho_{AB},\pi_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}\right) (6.42)
≤−log⁡[Tr⁡{ρA​B​πA⊗ρB}]2\displaystyle\leq-\log\left[\operatorname{Tr}\left\{\sqrt{\rho_{AB}}\sqrt{\pi_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}}\right\}\right]^{2} (6.43)
=log⁡|A|−log⁡[Tr⁡{ρA​B​IA⊗ρB}]2\displaystyle=\log\left|A\right|-\log\left[\operatorname{Tr}\left\{\sqrt{\rho_{AB}}\sqrt{I_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}}\right\}\right]^{2} (6.44)
=log⁡|A|−H1/2​(A|B)ρ\displaystyle=\log\left|A\right|-H_{1/2}\left(A|B\right)_{\rho} (6.45)
=log⁡|A|+H3/2​(A|C)ψ\displaystyle=\log\left|A\right|+H_{3/2}\left(A|C\right)_{\psi} (6.46)
≤log⁡|A|+H3/2​(A)ρ\displaystyle\leq\log\left|A\right|+H_{3/2}\left(A\right)_{\rho} (6.47)
≤2​log⁡|A|.\displaystyle\leq 2\log\left|A\right|. (6.48)

The reasons behind these steps are quite similar to those in the proof of Proposition 7, so we omit them.  

By making use of the special form of the entanglement fidelity for a quantum channel (see, e.g., [Wil13, Theorem 9.5.1]), we arrive at the following form for DF​(A¯,B)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) when evaluated for a pure state:

Proposition 32 (Pure states)

Let ψA​B\psi_{AB} be a pure state. Then

DF(A¯;B)ψ=−logsup|ϕx⟩,|φx⟩:∑x|φx⟩⟨φx|=I∑x|⟨φx|AψA|ϕx⟩A|2,D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\psi}=-\log\sup_{\left|\phi_{x}\right\rangle,\left|\varphi_{x}\right\rangle:\sum_{x}\left|\varphi_{x}\right\rangle\left\langle\varphi_{x}\right|=I}\sum_{x}\left|\left\langle\varphi_{x}\right|_{A}\psi_{A}\left|\phi_{x}\right\rangle_{A}\right|^{2}, (6.49)

where the optimization is over pure-state vectors |ϕx⟩\left|\phi_{x}\right\rangle and corresponding measurement vectors |φx⟩\left|\varphi_{x}\right\rangle satisfying ∑x|φx⟩⟨φx|=I\sum_{x}\left|\varphi_{x}\right\rangle\left\langle\varphi_{x}\right|=I.

Proposition 33 (Normalization)

The surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity DF​(A¯,B)ΦD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\Phi} is equal to log⁡d\log d for a maximally entangled state with Schmidt rank dd.

Proof. The following bound is a consequence of [Rai99, Lemma 2]

F⁡(ΦA​B,ℰA​(ΦA​B))≤1dF\left(\Phi_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\Phi_{AB}\right)\right)\leq\frac{1}{d} (6.50)

because ℰA​(ΦA​B)\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\Phi_{AB}\right) is a separable state. Since the bound holds for any entanglement breaking channel, we get

DF​(A¯,B)Φ≥log⁡d.D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\Phi}\geq\log d. (6.51)

On the other hand, an entanglement breaking channel ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} achieving this bound is one that dephases system AA in the Schmidt basis of ΦA​B\Phi_{AB}, so that

F⁡(ΦA​B,ℰA​(ΦA​B))\displaystyle F\left(\Phi_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\Phi_{AB}\right)\right) =⟨Φ|A​B(1d∑i|i⟩⟨i|A⊗|i⟩⟨i|B)|Φ⟩A​B\displaystyle=\left\langle\Phi\right|_{AB}\left(\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i}\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{A}\otimes\left|i\right\rangle\left\langle i\right|_{B}\right)\left|\Phi\right\rangle_{AB} (6.52)
=1d.\displaystyle=\frac{1}{d}. (6.53)

So this implies that DF​(A¯,B)Φ≤log⁡dD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\Phi}\leq\log d, which concludes the proof.  

Proposition 34 (Monotonicity)

The suprisal of measurement recovery fidelity is monotone with respect to quantum operations on the unmeasured system, i.e.,

DF​(A¯,B)ρ≥DF​(A¯,B′)σ,D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}\geq D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B^{\prime}\right)_{\sigma}, (6.54)

where σA​B′≡𝒩B→B′​(ρA​B)\sigma_{AB^{\prime}}\equiv\mathcal{N}_{B\rightarrow B^{\prime}}\left(\rho_{AB}\right).

Proof. Intuitively, this follows because it is easier to recover from a measurement the noisier that a state is to begin with. Indeed, let ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} be an entanglement breaking channel. Then

F⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))\displaystyle F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right) ≤F⁡(σA​B′,ℰA​(σA​B′))\displaystyle\leq F\left(\sigma_{AB^{\prime}},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\sigma_{AB^{\prime}}\right)\right) (6.55)
≤supℰAF⁡(σA​B′,ℰA​(σA​B′)),\displaystyle\leq\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\sigma_{AB^{\prime}},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\sigma_{AB^{\prime}}\right)\right), (6.56)

where the first inequality is due to the fact that ℰA\mathcal{E}_{A} commutes with 𝒩B→B′\mathcal{N}_{B\rightarrow B^{\prime}} and monotonicity of the fidelity under quantum operations. Since the inequality holds for all entanglement breaking channels, we can conclude that

supℰAF⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))≤supℰAF⁡(σA​B′,ℰA​(σA​B′)).\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)\leq\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\sigma_{AB^{\prime}},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\sigma_{AB^{\prime}}\right)\right). (6.57)

Taking a negative logarithm gives the statement of the proposition.  

With a proof nearly identical to that for Proposition 25, we find that DF​(A¯,B)ρD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho} is continuous:

Proposition 35 (Continuity)

DF​(A¯,B)D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right) is a continuous function of its input. That is, given two bipartite states ρA​B\rho_{AB} and σA​B\sigma_{AB} such that F⁡(ρA​B,σA​B)≥1−εF\left(\rho_{AB},\sigma_{AB}\right)\geq 1-\varepsilon where ε∈[0,1]\varepsilon\in\left[0,1\right], then the following inequalities hold

|supℰAF⁡(ρA​B,ℰA​(ρA​B))−supℰAF⁡(σA​B,ℰA​(σA​B))|\displaystyle\left|\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\rho_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\rho_{AB}\right)\right)-\sup_{\mathcal{E}_{A}}F\left(\sigma_{AB},\mathcal{E}_{A}\left(\sigma_{AB}\right)\right)\right| ≤8​ε,\displaystyle\leq 8\sqrt{\varepsilon}, (6.58)
|DF​(A¯,B)ρ−DF​(A¯,B)σ|\displaystyle\left|D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}-D_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\sigma}\right| ≤|A|2​8​ε.\displaystyle\leq\left|A\right|^{2}8\sqrt{\varepsilon}. (6.59)

7 Multipartite fidelity of recovery

We state here that it is certainly possible to generalize the fidelity of recovery to the multipartite setting. Indeed, by following the same line of reasoning mentioned in the introduction (starting from the Rényi conditional multipartite information [BSW14, Section 10.1] and understanding the α=1/2\alpha=1/2 quantity in terms of several Petz recovery maps), we can define the multipartite fidelity of recovery for a multipartite state ρA1⋯AlC\rho_{A_{1}\cdots A_{l}C} as follows:

F(A1;A2;⋯;Al|C)ρ=supℛC→A1​C1,…,ℛC→Al−1​Cl−1F(ρA1⋯AlC,ℛC→A1​C1∘⋯∘ℛC→Al−1​Cl−1(ρAl​C)).F\left(A_{1};A_{2};\cdots;A_{l}|C\right)_{\rho}=\sup_{\mathcal{R}_{C\rightarrow A_{1}C}^{1},\ldots,\mathcal{R}_{C\rightarrow A_{l-1}C}^{l-1}}F\left(\rho_{A_{1}\cdots A_{l}C},\mathcal{R}_{C\rightarrow A_{1}C}^{1}\circ\cdots\circ\mathcal{R}_{C\rightarrow A_{l-1}C}^{l-1}\left(\rho_{A_{l}C}\right)\right). (7.1)

The interpretation of this quantity is as written: systems A1A_{1} through Al−1A_{l-1} of the state ρA1⋯AlC\rho_{A_{1}\cdots A_{l}C} are lost, and one attempts to recover them one at a time by performing a sequence of recovery maps on system CC alone. We can then define a quantity analogous to the multipartite conditional mutual information as follows:

IF​(A1;A2;⋯;Al|C)ρ≡−log⁡F​(A1;A2;⋯;Al|C)ρ,I_{F}\left(A_{1};A_{2};\cdots;A_{l}|C\right)_{\rho}\equiv-\log F\left(A_{1};A_{2};\cdots;A_{l}|C\right)_{\rho}, (7.2)

and one can easily show along the lines given here for the bipartite case that the resulting quantity is non-negative, monotone under local operations, and obeys a dimension bound.

We leave it as an open question to develop fully a multipartite geometric squashed entanglement, defined by replacing the conditional multipartite mutual information in the usual definition [YHH+09] with IFI_{F} given above.

8 Conclusion

We have defined the fidelity of recovery F​(A;B|C)ρF\left(A;B|C\right)_{\rho} of a tripartite state ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} to quantify how well one can recover the full state on all three systems if system AA is lost and the recovery map can act only on system CC. By taking the negative logarithm of the fidelity of recovery, we obtain an entropic quantity IF​(A;B|C)ρI_{F}\left(A;B|C\right)_{\rho} which obeys nearly all of the entropic relations that the conditional mutual information does (non-negativity, monotonicity under local operations, duality, and dimension bounds). The quantities F​(A;B|C)ρF\left(A;B|C\right)_{\rho} and IF​(A;B|C)ρI_{F}\left(A;B|C\right)_{\rho} are rooted in our earlier work on seeking out Rényi generationalizations of the conditional mutual information [BSW14]. Whereas we have not been able to prove that all of the aforementioned properties hold for the Rényi conditional mutual informations from [BSW14], it is pleasing to us that it is relatively straightforward to show that these properties hold for IF​(A;B|C)ρI_{F}\left(A;B|C\right)_{\rho}.

Another contribution was to define a geometric squashed entanglement measure EFsq​(A,B)ρE_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho}, inspired by the original squashed entanglement measure from [CW04]. We proved that EFsq​(A,B)ρE_{F}^{\operatorname{sq}}\left(A;B\right)_{\rho} is an entanglement monotone, is faithful, reduces to a variant of the well known geometric measure of entanglement [WG03, CAH14], normalized on maximally entangled states, subadditive, and continuous. The new entanglement measure could find applications in “one-shot” scenarios of quantum information theory, since it is fundamentally a one-shot measure based on the fidelity.

Our final contribution was to define the surprisal of measurement recovery fidelity DF​(A¯,B)ρD_{F}\left(\overline{A};B\right)_{\rho}, a quantum correlation measure having physical roots in the same vein as those used to justify the definition of the quantum discord. We showed that it is non-negative, invariant under local isometries, faithful on classical-quantum states, obeys a dimension bound, and is continuous. Furthermore, we used this quantity to characterize quantum states with discord nearly equal to zero, finding that such states are approximate fixed points of an entanglement breaking channel.

From here, there are several interesting lines of inquiry to pursue. Can we prove a stronger chain rule for the fidelity of recovery? If something along these lines holds, it might be helpful in establishing that the geometric squashed entanglement is monogamous. Can we use geometric squashed entanglement to characterize the one-shot distillable entanglement or secret key of a bipartite state? Is it possible to improve our continuity bounds? Can one show that geometric squashed entanglement is nonlockable [Chr06]? Preliminary evidence from considering the strongest known locking schemes from [FHS11] suggests that it might not be lockable. We are also interested in a multipartite geometric squashed entanglement, but we face similar challenges as those discussed in [LW14] for establishing its faithfulness.
